fieldNotes.truckGate: The Jif plant is a fully fenced urban complex. Street View along the internal access road off Winchester Rd shows chain-link / ornamental perimeter fencing and rolling gates at the access points (rail-crossing gate visible open). Trucks enter through a controlled gated point.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth positively identified at the truck driveway off Winchester Rd despite checking multiple Street View headings (2024-2025). Signage at the office entrance reads NO TRACTOR TRAILERS, directing trucks to a separate gate; that gate appears to be a rolling fence gate without a staffed booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true: a controlled truck gate exists but no guard shack was found, implying kiosk/call-box/app check-in. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: The internal access road off Winchester Rd is short before it reaches dock aprons and the yard; only 1-2 trucks of stacking room.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Tight urban site jammed against Winchester Rd (a major divided arterial) with a rail line; a truck queue at the gate has little room and could spill toward the road.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Visible dock faces show ~12-14 trailers backed in on each of multiple building faces; the world's-largest Jif plant spans ~28 acres / multiple buildings, putting the total in the 25-50 band (overhead estimate).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Multiple large trailer-storage lots on the west/northwest of the complex, 80+ trailers visible, capacity well above 50.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: At least one main internal truck driveway off Winchester Rd plus a rail-side gate; counted 2, low confidence.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Confirmed campus of 9+ interconnected buildings (process plant, warehouses, office) across ~28 acres per web sources.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail spur runs into the plant; Jif-branded silo and rail tracks visible in Street View.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Site is within dense Lexington urban fabric — residential, commercial and arterial roads on all sides.
